_comment: Tier ladder and per-source capability map. Reorder here rather than in code.
Tier names must match fetchpdf.retrieval.tiers.Tier members.
'requires' lists IdentifierSet fields that must be non-empty for the source
to be attempted at all -- this is what keeps quota-limited calls off records
that could never have used them.

No 'host' key on sources: rate limiting buckets on the actual URL host inside HttpClient, so a per-source host was inert config that looked like a knob. Adjust throttling in rate_limits below, keyed by real hostname.
_ladders_comment: T6 plain text is 4th for screening and ABSENT for extraction. Flattened text
keeps every number but anchors none of them to a row or column, so an
extraction model produces confident, plausible, wrong arm-to-outcome
assignments. That is worse than a missing table, so extraction refuses it
outright rather than ranking it last and degrading into it.

europepmc_xml.notes: Highest-value T1 route. Gated on search flags, but tolerates 404 anyway: ~12% of records with a PMCID are not in the EPMC OA subset.

preprint_jats.notes: bioRxiv/medRxiv JATS. Also the route for EPMC PPR records, whose availability flags say full text exists when it does not.

pmc_efetch.notes: FALLBACK ONLY -- same underlying PMC JATS as Europe PMC. Never stored alongside it; two copies of one source is not corroboration.

elsevier_tdm.notes: Entitlement- and IP-bound. Non-entitled requests return 200 with an error payload, so the validator, not the status code, decides.

crossref_tdm.notes: link[] with content-type text/xml AND intended-application text-mining. Crossref retired click-through tokens in Dec 2020, so 401/403 is the expected case, not an error.

unpaywall_html.notes: oa_locations[].url is sometimes XML or HTML full text rather than a PDF. publishedVersion preferred over acceptedVersion.

publisher_html.notes: DOI resolution to publisher full text. At most OA publishers this HTML is generated from the same JATS as the XML endpoint.

arxiv_html.notes: Official arxiv.org/html covers ~Dec 2023 onward; ar5iv covers the back catalogue to 2007 (verified: 0704.0001 -> 200, 35 tables). Enabled because between them they cover effectively the whole corpus. Machine conversion, so the caveat is recorded in provenance.

arxiv_eprint.notes: LaTeX source tarball. arXiv tightened rate limits in Feb 2026 -- this host gets its own slow bucket.

europepmc_supplements.notes: Keyed on the PMCID already resolved in phase 1, so cheaper than enumerating repositories.

legacy_pdf_chain.notes: One call into the existing chain in fetch_pdf_from_doi. Preserves its retries, backoff and Playwright paths by construction rather than by duplication.

elsevier_pdf.notes: Same endpoint as elsevier_tdm, asked with Accept: application/pdf. Entitlement is per-representation at Elsevier, so a record whose XML view is coredata-only or a 400-char corrigendum often still serves the full typeset PDF. Ordered after legacy_pdf_chain because the chain's routes cost no Elsevier quota.

core_fulltext.notes: Always stamped tables_unavailable=true. Refuses to return anything when target_task is extraction.

landing_page.notes: Last resort. Recorded so a record that produced nothing usable is distinguishable from one never attempted.

rate_limits._comment: Per-host, never global: configured limits differ by more than an order of magnitude across these APIs. rps_keyed applies when key_env is set in the environment.
_supplementary_comment: --pull-supplementary fetches files rather than metadata, so it talks to a
second set of hosts: the CDNs and file endpoints the listing APIs point at.
Without entries here they all fall to _default, which is safe but treats a
publisher CDN and a scraped article page as equally robust. S3 is fast and
does not care; article pages and supp.apa.org are scraped one at a time.

thresholds._comment: Character counts are of extracted body text, not raw bytes.
